questions.question: Gurpurab is celebrated by which of the following community?
questions.solution:
Gurpurab, also known as Guru Nanak Gurpurab, is one of the most sacred festivals celebrated by the Sikh community.
  • It marks the birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru, Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
  • The celebration typically involves Prabhat Pheris (early morning processions), Akhand Path (non-stop reading of the Guru Granth Sahib), and Langar (community kitchen).
  • Note: The term 'Gurpurab' is used to refer to any festival associated with the lives of the Sikh Gurus.

questions.question: Pushkar Camel fair is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Pushkar Camel Fair (Pushkar Mela) is a world-famous annual multi-day livestock fair and cultural fete held in Rajasthan.
  • It takes place in the town of Pushkar (Ajmer district) on the banks of the Pushkar Lake.
  • It is one of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, attracting thousands of tourists and traders.
  • Additional Info: The fair coincides with the Hindu festival of Kartik Purnima, where devotees take a holy dip in the lake.

questions.question: Rann Utsav promotes natural beauty and other famous traveling places of the stunning zone of _________ . During the full moon nights in the winter season, the white sand desert looks more mesmerizing.
questions.solution:
Rann Utsav is a vibrant cultural festival that celebrates the natural beauty of the Kutch region in Gujarat.
  • The festival is famous for the White Desert (Great Rann of Kutch), which is composed of salt marshes.
  • During Full Moon nights, the salt crust reflects the moonlight, creating a surreal and mesmerizing landscape.
  • Note: The festival highlights Kutchi handicrafts, folk music, dance, and traditional cuisine.

questions.question: During which religious event in India do devotees take a holy dip in the Ganges River, believing it washes away their sins, and perform various rituals at the riverbanks?
questions.solution:
The Kumbh Mela is the largest peaceful gathering in the world, where devotees congregate to take a holy dip in sacred rivers like the Ganges.
  • Believed to cleanse one of all sins, the dip is taken at four main locations: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain.
  • The festival is held every 12 years (Maha Kumbh) at each location, determined by astrological positions of Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon.
  • Fact: In 2017, the Kumbh Mela was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
